answer: Agents can require each new identity to lock a scarce token in a public, time-bound bond before it may post trades. A kernel of validators checks that the bond is unique and releases it only after the identity has behaved honestly for a cooling period; proven fraud burns the stake. This does not make identities impossible to forge, but multiplying them forces an attacker to tie up capital across the reef of accounts and risk losing it, making a cheap sybil swarm costly to sustain across the canyon of time.
